newsitem.title: JAPAN: Japan non-bank to seek liquidation.
newsitem.headline: Japan non-bank to seek liquidation.

text.p: A Japanese non-bank lender with debts of 259.4 billion yen ($2.27 billion) said on Thursday it would seek liquidation, just days after two big brokerages announced billion-dollar bailouts for struggling subsidiaries.

Koei Corp, of which the Industrial Bank of Japan Ltd (IBJ) is a major creditor, built up its debts with years of aggressive real estate lending. It will seek liquidation under court protection by the end of March.

On Wednesday, Yamaichi Securities Co announced it would spend 150 billion yen ($1.31 billion) to bail out a non-bank subsidiary. A day earlier, Nikko Securities Co said it would earmark 147.5 billion yen ($1.29 billion) to help three affiliated firms clear up bad debts.

The bailout schemes by Yamaichi and Nikko, both of which were forced to trim their earnings forecasts for the year to next March, followed earlier bailout schemes announced by Nomura Securities Co and Daiwa Securities Co.
The measures underlined the scope of the bad debt problem faced by Japan's financial industry, which analysts say will still require years to recover from an estimated $400 billion in bad loans.
The bad debt is mainly from excessive real estate lending in the heady 1980s "bubble" era of inflated asset prices.
"It is true that we will go in that direction (to seek liquidation). We will probably apply to the Tokyo District Court for special liquidation by the end of March," a Koei official said.
An IBJ spokesman said Koei had informed the bank of its liquidation plan and that the bank would agree to the plan.
IBJ's outstanding loans to Koei total 61.2 billion yen ($536 million), a Koei official said.
Koei's other creditors include Sumitomo Trust and Banking Co Ltd, which has outstanding loans of 9.6 billion yen ($84.2 million) to Koei, the Koei official said.
Koei will also seek approval for its liquidation plans from its other creditor banks, the official said.

The company, suffering from aggressive lending for real estate projects, decided to seek liquidation because it will have completed a five-year restructuring programme in February, the Koei official said.
"We will have completed selling the properties we planned to sell under the restructuring programme," the Koei official said.
The amounts earned from the sales will not be as large as originally expected due to the sluggish real estate market, he said. ($1=114 yen)
